title: A scoped decision is handed to the reader as context, not a step
intention: A ticket's decisions that describe the voyage or the session rather than the build reach the rehearsal reader as context it reads, not as steps it must judge, because a scope line marks them so through the rehearsal door.
why: Akien answered open-dcfd67f37318 '(a)': cast a reader ticket that makes a scope line bind structurally — a decide line can mark decisions out of the build's scope, and render() hands those to the reader as context, not as steps to judge. Measured: 41202d4c8d3b ran 12 passes with gaps 2 -> 6 -> 8 as prose scope lines were added; b4d39f3610f3 (2026-10-08) read D6/D7 gaps while its reader's own would_settle said 'This ticket's build scope ends at D5 (per D9)', and retire was refused because D9 cited them.
traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel: 8y spent 12 passes and b4d3 two re-judging decisions every reader's would_settle already called out of scope) and CP4 (rehearsal is paid per pass; a scope note in prose did not bind the reader, n=2 on 41202d4c8d3b and b4d39f3610f3).
how: cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py gains scope(ticket, ns, *, by, because) beside retire(): each named live decision gains context = {by, at, because} through the door's cast verb and keeps its text. reader_view moves every context-stamped decision out of the pasted copy's decisions into a top-level 'context' list (each text still labeled D<n>), and decision_ids_of leaves them out, so a read need not and may not name them as steps. cairn/machines/rehearsal/__main__.py gains --scope D<n> [D<n> ...] --because "<why>" --by <who>, standing alone like --retire. prompt.md gains one line: the 'context' list is read for what it says and is never a step. One new proof.

decisions.text: cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py gains scope(ticket, ns, *, by, because, root=None) directly after retire(), mirroring it: it collects every lack and raises Refused("scope refused over {ticket} — N lack(s): ...") naming all of them, writing nothing — lacks are a missing --by, an empty because, no ids, an id the ticket does not carry, an id already scoped (has context), an id already retired, and a line whose by differs from the caller (fold(d.get('by')) != fold(by)). It has no citation check: a scoped line stays visible to the reader. On pass it sets d['context'] = {'by': by, 'at': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec='seconds'), 'because': because} on each named decision, keeps its text unchanged, writes through _write_ticket(tk, doc, why=...) (door verb cast), and returns the list of scoped decision dicts.
decisions.step: unlisted: scope() function to stamp context={by, at, because} on named live decisions through door verb cast

decisions.text: reader_view in rehearsal.py keeps its current work (drop retired, label each text D<n>, add the [settled by D<n>] annotations) over the live decisions, then splits them: every decision carrying a 'context' field moves out of doc['decisions'] into doc['context'], in the same order, its text still labeled D<n>; doc['context'] is set only when that list is non-empty, so a ticket with nothing scoped reads byte-identical to today.
decisions.step: unlisted: reader_view moves scoped decisions into a top-level 'context' list

decisions.text: decision_ids_of in rehearsal.py omits every decision carrying a 'context' field, exactly as it already omits 'retired' ones; validate() is unchanged, since it already refuses a step naming an id outside decision_ids and requires every carried id once.
decisions.step: unlisted: decision_ids_of omits scoped decision ids

decisions.text: cairn/machines/rehearsal/__main__.py adds --scope (nargs='+', metavar 'D<n>') beside --retire, reusing the existing --because and --by flags. A --scope branch mirrors the --retire branch: p.error (exit 2) if combined with --decide, --proved, --standing or --retire, or if --by or --because is missing — so nothing is written; each id parses through _decision_id; it calls R.scope(args.ticket, ns, by=args.by, because=args.because), prints 'scoped D{n} on {ticket} by {by}: {text}' per returned decision and then 'the ticket's bytes changed — rehearse again before BUILDME', and returns 0; a Refused prints its message and returns 2. The usage epilog gains the line: cairn rehearse <ticket> --scope D<n> [D<n> ...] --because "<why>" --by <who>.
decisions.step: unlisted: CLI gains --scope D<n> [...] --because <why> --by <who>, standing alone like --retire

decisions.text: cairn/machines/rehearsal/prompt.md gains one bullet in its Rules section, directly after the 'Name steps by decision id' bullet, verbatim: '- **The `context` list is never a step.** A decision there was scoped by its author: it describes the voyage or the session, not the build. Read it for what it says, and never emit a node for it — its id is not in the vocabulary, and a reading that names it is handed back.'
